title: Technology audit — Core trading and order management systems and 4 more

intake.note: Order management platform migrated to cloud in Q2. Vendor now controls patching.

scopeSummary: This audit covers privileged access, vulnerability remediation, cloud configuration and recovery testing across the order management platform and its market-connectivity systems, weighted towards the control boundaries that moved during the Q2 cloud migration.

riskFactors.factor: Vendor-controlled patching leaves the firm unable to meet its own remediation window
riskFactors.rationale: Where the vendor schedules patching, the firm's remediation clock runs on someone else's calendar. A critical vulnerability disclosed on a Friday is exposed until the vendor's next window, and the contract may not give the firm any right to accelerate it.

riskFactors.factor: Privileged access to the trading platform is shared and held by third parties
riskFactors.rationale: A shared administrator account used by vendor engineers cannot be traced to a named individual, so an unauthorised change cannot be attributed after the fact. Access reviews overdue means nobody has confirmed recently who still holds these credentials.

riskFactors.factor: Cloud migration moved the control boundary without moving the obligation
drivenBy: Core trading and order management systems
riskFactors.rationale: Under the shared responsibility model the provider secures the platform and the firm secures what it puts on it, but the licence obligations sit entirely with the firm. A migration performed under time pressure typically leaves configuration hardening as an open item.

riskFactors.factor: Untested recovery on a system with a regulatory downtime cap
drivenBy: Disaster recovery not tested, or tests failed
riskFactors.rationale: MAS caps unscheduled downtime for a critical system, and a recovery plan that has not been exercised is an assumption rather than a control. Market connectivity failure during a trading session has no acceptable degraded mode.

riskFactors.factor: Customer personal data processed outside Singapore without evidenced transfer conditions
riskFactors.rationale: Transferring personal data overseas requires the firm to satisfy itself the recipient offers comparable protection. A cloud region selected for latency or cost is unlikely to have been assessed against that test.

riskFactors.factor: Access recertification has lapsed across the estate
riskFactors.rationale: Overdue recertification means leavers and movers accumulate entitlements nobody has confirmed they still need. Combined with remote access this widens the window in which a dormant account can be used without being noticed.

obligations.requirement: Grant access on a need-to-have basis, enforce accountability for privileged accounts, and review user access rights periodically.

obligations.reference: MAS Notice on Cyber Hygiene — Administrative Accounts
obligations.requirement: Restrict administrative accounts to authorised persons, and ensure they are not used for routine activity.

obligations.reference: MAS Notice on Cyber Hygiene — Security Patches
obligations.requirement: Apply security patches to address vulnerabilities to every system, within a timeframe commensurate with the risk posed.

obligations.reference: MAS TRM Guidelines — Systems Reliability, Availability and Recoverability
obligations.requirement: Establish recovery objectives for critical systems and validate them through periodic testing that includes a failover to the recovery site.

obligations.reference: MAS Outsourcing Guidelines — Monitoring and Control
obligations.requirement: Maintain oversight of material outsourcing arrangements, including the right to audit the service provider and to be notified of incidents affecting the firm.
Assess and manage the risks of cloud adoption, including the allocation of responsibilities between the firm and the cloud service provider.
Make reasonable security arrangements to protect personal data in the organisation's possession or control.
Do not transfer personal data outside Singapore unless the recipient is bound by legally enforceable obligations to provide a comparable standard of protection.
Subject changes to production systems to authorisation, testing and approval commensurate with their risk and impact.

scopeAreas.title: Privileged and vendor access to the order management platform
scopeAreas.rationale: Shared administrator credentials held by vendor engineers on a business-critical trading system, with recertification overdue, is the combination most likely to produce an unattributable change during this audit period.

steps.procedure: Export the full list of accounts with administrator or equivalent privilege on the order management platform directly from the identity system, and trace each to a named individual and an approved access request.
steps.evidenceRequired: Privileged account inventory exported by the auditor, and the approval record for each account.
steps.sampling: Full population of privileged accounts — the population is small enough to test entirely.

steps.procedure: For each vendor engineer holding access, inspect the contractual basis for that access and confirm the account is individually named rather than shared.
steps.evidenceRequired: The outsourcing agreement's access clauses and the account listing filtered to vendor personnel.

steps.procedure: Reperform the most recent access recertification for the platform and compare the reviewer's conclusions against the entitlements actually in force on the review date.
steps.evidenceRequired: The completed recertification pack with reviewer sign-off, and a point-in-time entitlement extract for that date.
steps.sampling: The most recent completed cycle; if none falls in the period, record that as the finding.

steps.procedure: Trace privileged session activity for a sample of days to the individual who performed it, using system-generated session logs rather than a summary report.
steps.evidenceRequired: Raw privileged session logs for the sampled dates.
steps.sampling: 10 trading days selected across the period, including at least two days following a production change.

scopeAreas.title: Vulnerability remediation where the vendor controls the patch window
scopeAreas.rationale: The firm carries the remediation obligation but not the schedule. This area tests whether the contract and the operating practice actually let the firm meet its own timeframe.

steps.procedure: Inspect the outsourcing agreement for the firm's right to require patching within a defined timeframe, and for its right to be notified of vulnerabilities affecting the hosted platform.
steps.evidenceRequired: The executed agreement and any service schedule covering security maintenance.

steps.procedure: Trace each critical vulnerability disclosed during the period against the platform to the date it was remediated, and recalculate the elapsed time against the firm's own stated remediation window.
steps.evidenceRequired: Vulnerability scan output or vendor advisories for the period, and the patch deployment records.
steps.sampling: Full population of critical-rated vulnerabilities; a random sample of 15 high-rated ones.

steps.procedure: Inspect the escalation record for any vulnerability that exceeded the window, and confirm it reached the technology risk committee rather than stopping at the platform team.
steps.evidenceRequired: Committee minutes and the exception register.
steps.sampling: All instances identified in the step above.

scopeAreas.title: Cloud configuration and the shared responsibility boundary post-migration
scopeAreas.rationale: The platform moved in Q2 under a delivery deadline. This area tests whether the firm's half of the responsibility model was hardened and documented, rather than assumed to be the provider's.

steps.procedure: Obtain the cloud provider's shared responsibility matrix for the services in use and trace each firm-side control to a named owner and a documented configuration standard.
steps.evidenceRequired: The provider's responsibility matrix and the firm's cloud security standard.
steps.sampling: Full population of services supporting the order management platform.

steps.procedure: Export the current configuration of the production environment and compare it against the firm's hardening baseline, recording every deviation.
steps.evidenceRequired: Configuration export pulled by the auditor from the provider's console or API, and the approved baseline.
steps.sampling: Full-population configuration comparison — automated tooling makes a sample unnecessary.

steps.procedure: Inspect the migration's go-live approval and confirm that open security items were either closed or formally accepted by a named risk owner before cutover.
steps.evidenceRequired: The go-live decision record and the open-items register as at the cutover date.

scopeAreas.title: Recovery testing for market-connectivity systems
scopeAreas.rationale: A regulatory downtime cap applies and the recovery plan has not been exercised since the migration changed the topology it was written against.

steps.procedure: Inspect the recovery objectives documented for each market-connectivity system and confirm they were reapproved after the migration changed the topology.
steps.evidenceRequired: The business impact analysis and the recovery plan with its approval date.

steps.procedure: Observe or reperform a failover test, or where none has been run in the period, obtain written confirmation of that fact from the Head of Infrastructure.
steps.evidenceRequired: The test report with its exceptions, or the written confirmation that no test was performed.
steps.sampling: The most recent test; absence of one is itself the result.

steps.procedure: Recalculate actual unscheduled downtime for the period from incident records and compare it against the regulatory cap.
steps.evidenceRequired: The incident register and system availability reports for the period.

scopeAreas.title: Cross-border processing of customer personal data
scopeAreas.rationale: Cloud regions were selected during migration. This area tests whether transfer conditions were assessed before customer data began being processed outside Singapore.

scopeAreas.title: Change authorisation for frequent production releases
scopeAreas.rationale: A continuous deployment cadence on a system executing financial transactions puts weight on automated gates rather than on a change advisory board.

runs.produced: 6 risk factors across 5 dimensions, from 22 intake selections
notes: Dropped "End-user computing exposure" — no mechanism explained.
